name: Colombo
heading: Adobe and AI training in Colombo
summary: Instructor-led Adobe Creative Cloud and AI classes taught in person in Colombo, on live files, priced in LKR and invoiced to Sri Lankan employers.
body_html:
Colombo is where MyLearnPlus is based and where our classroom dates run. The people who sit in these rooms are mostly working: designers in agencies and studios, in-house marketing and communications staff at apparel exporters, banks, telecommunications companies and hotel groups, production and creative teams inside the BPO and shared services sector, and a steady number of freelancers and final-year students who need to be employable in a specific piece of software by a specific month. The problems they arrive with are concrete. A self-taught designer needs to hand over a layered Photoshop file that a colleague can still edit. A marketing executive has been told to bring video editing in-house. A print buyer is moving a catalogue off Word and into InDesign. A team has started using generative AI without anyone agreeing what may be published.

A classroom day is one person per machine and one file per person. You work on your own laptop wherever possible, so the presets, brushes, fonts, templates and finished files you build in class leave the room with you rather than staying on a training machine. We check that Creative Cloud or the relevant tool is installed and licensed before the first session, and we run a setup check for anyone who wants help with it. The instructor teaches from a screen at working resolution, then walks the room while you do the same task on your own work, which is the part of a classroom day that live online cannot fully replace. The venue address is {to be confirmed}, and the room, parking and building access details go out with your joining instructions.

Getting there is a real consideration in Colombo, so we set start and finish times against the morning and evening peaks rather than against a template, and each date on the schedule shows its own times. Learners commonly travel in from Gampaha, Negombo, Moratuwa, Kalutara and further, by rail into Fort or Maradana, by bus, or by ride-hailing. Two-day and three-day courses are run on consecutive days for that reason: it is cheaper to make the journey twice in a row than four times across a month. If you do miss a session, the recording of the class is available to you for twelve months and every live booking includes one free repeat of the same class.

What the Colombo market asks for is fairly consistent. Prices for learners and organisations in Sri Lanka are quoted and charged in LKR, not converted from a dollar rate at checkout. Employers can be invoiced against a purchase order, and once a team reaches roughly five people a private class on the same syllabus, run in your own office or at our venue, is usually the cheaper and more useful buy because the exercises can be swapped for your own brand, your own photography and your own documents. Weekend and evening cohorts appear on the schedule where there is demand for them, which there usually is from people who cannot take two working days out.

Certification matters more here than it does in some markets, because a lot of Colombo work is sold to clients abroad and a credential is evidence a stranger will accept. Be clear about how it works: the Adobe Certified Professional exams are set by Adobe and delivered through Certiport at authorised test centres, the voucher is bought separately, and no training provider can award the certification or promise you a pass. What we do is teach the courses against the published exam objectives, tell you honestly which exam maps to which course, and finish the relevant classes with a timed practice task. If a Colombo classroom date does not suit you, the same syllabus runs live online with the same materials and the same instructors, and much of the catalogue is also available self-paced.
